entities.name: Agnelo Rossi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agnelo Rossi (1913–1995) was a Brazilian cardinal and Archbishop of São Paulo who later became a senior official of the Roman Curia, making him one of the most influential figures in the global Church in the 1970s–1980s. Born in Joaquim Egídio, São Paulo state, he was ordained a priest in 1937 and became Archbishop of Aparecida before his appointment to São Paulo in 1964.

As Archbishop of São Paulo (1964–1970), Rossi led Brazil's most important archdiocese during a critical moment: the 1964 military coup had installed a dictatorship, and the Church faced the question of how to respond to authoritarian rule and social injustice. Rossi's tenure at São Paulo was more conservative than that of his successor Dom Paulo Arns, and he was transferred to Rome in 1970, where he served as Prefect of the Congregation for the Evangelisation of Peoples (Propaganda Fide) until 1984—one of the most powerful positions in the Vatican.

As head of Propaganda Fide, Rossi directed the global missionary enterprise of the Catholic Church at its most expansive period, overseeing mission territories across Africa, Asia, and Oceania. He was elevated to cardinal in 1965 by Paul VI. His career trajectory—from Brazilian bishop to global mission administrator—embodied the internationalisation of the Roman Curia in the post-conciliar era.
